title.zh: 卷51 列傳第16 長孫覽
title.raw: 卷51 列傳第16 長孫覽 Volume 51 Biographies 16: Zhang Sunlan

sentences.zh: 長孫覽長孫覽，字休因，河南洛陽人也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Lan—Zhangsun Lan, courtesy name Xiuyin, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Lan, whose courtesy name was Xiuyin, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖稚，魏太師、假黃鉞、上党文宣王。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi had been Grand Preceptor of Wei, holder of the provisional yellow battle-axe, and Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi had served as the Northern Wei's Grand Preceptor, held the provisional yellow battle-axe, and bore the title Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 父紹遠，周小宗伯、上党郡公。

translations.literal: His father Shaoyuan had been Junior Director of the Imperial Clan of Zhou and Duke of Shangdang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shaoyuan had been the Northern Zhou's Junior Director of the Imperial Clan and Duke of Shangdang commandery.

sentences.zh: 覽性弘雅，有器量，略涉書記，尤曉鐘律。

translations.literal: Lan was magnanimous and refined in character, possessed capacity and measure, had a slight acquaintance with written records, and was especially versed in pitch pipes and musical scales.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was open and elegant in temperament, had breadth of mind, knew something of clerical work, and was particularly skilled in pitch pipes and musical theory.

sentences.zh: 魏大統中，起家東宮親信。

translations.literal: In the Datong era of Northern Wei he first entered service as an intimate attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: During the Northern Wei's Datong era he began his career as an intimate attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 周明帝時，為大都督。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou he served as Grand Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming of Northern Zhou he held the post of Grand Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 武帝在籓，與覽親善，及即位，彌加禮焉，超拜車騎大將軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Xiang was still in his fief, he was on friendly terms with Lan; after he took the throne his courtesy toward him increased, and Lan was promoted in one step to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: While Yuwen Yong was still heir apparent he was close to Lan; once he became emperor he treated him with even greater honor and promoted him at a stroke to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 每公卿上奏，必令省讀。

translations.literal: Whenever the high ministers submitted memorials, the emperor always had Lan read them over.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever ministers of state presented memorials, the emperor invariably had Lan review them first.

sentences.zh: 覽有口辯，聲氣雄壯，凡所宣傳，百僚屬目，帝每嘉歎之。

translations.literal: Lan had eloquence; his voice and bearing were imposing; whatever he announced, the hundred officials fixed their eyes upon him, and the emperor often praised and sighed over him.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was a gifted speaker with a powerful voice; whenever he delivered an imperial message the entire court watched him, and the emperor repeatedly expressed his admiration.

sentences.zh: 覽初名善，帝謂之曰：「朕以萬機，委卿先覽。」

translations.literal: Lan's original name had been Shan. The emperor said to him, "I entrust the myriad affairs of state to you for prior review."
translations.idiomatic: Lan had originally been named Shan. The emperor told him, "I am placing the weight of government upon you to review matters first."

sentences.zh: 遂賜名焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bestowed the new name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: With that he gave him his present name.

sentences.zh: 及誅宇文護，以功進封薛國公。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu was executed, for his merit he was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Hu was killed, Lan was raised to Duke of Xue for his part in the plot.

sentences.zh: 其後曆小司空。

translations.literal: Thereafter he successively held the post of Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as Junior Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 從平齊，進位柱國，封第二子寬管國公。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign to pacify Qi, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his second son Kuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Guan state.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the conquest of Northern Qi, was promoted to Pillar of State, and his second son Kuan was enfeoffed as Duke of Guan.

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，進位上柱國、大司徒，俄曆同、涇二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education, and soon afterward successively governed the two prefectures of Tong and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan he rose to Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Minister of Education, and before long served in succession as governor of Tong and Jing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 高祖為丞相，轉宜州刺史。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor was Chancellor, Lan was transferred to Governor of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Lan was reassigned as governor of Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，將有事於江南，征為東南道行軍元帥，統八總管出壽陽，水陸俱進。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, as preparations were being made for operations in the Jiangnan region, he was summoned as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, commanding eight area commanders out of Shouyang, advancing by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 2 (582), with war planned against the south, he was appointed campaigning commander-in-chief of the Southeast Circuit, leading eight area commanders from Shouyang in a combined land-and-water advance.

sentences.zh: 師臨江，陳人大駭。

translations.literal: When the army reached the Yangtze, the people of Chen were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: As his forces approached the Yangtze, the Chen court was thrown into panic.

sentences.zh: 會陳宣帝卒，覽欲乘釁遂滅之，監軍高熲以禮不伐喪而還。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Xuan of Chen died; Lan wished to seize the opportunity and destroy Chen, but the supervising general Gao Hui, citing the rule that one does not attack during mourning, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan of Chen died, Lan wanted to exploit the moment and destroy Chen outright, but the supervising commander Gao Hui held that one must not campaign during a period of mourning and pulled the army back.

sentences.zh: 上常命覽與安德王雄、上柱國元諧、李充、左僕射高熲、右衛大將軍虞慶則、吳州總管賀若弼等同宴，上曰：「朕昔在周朝，備展誠節，但苦猜忌，每致寒心。

translations.literal: The emperor often ordered Lan to feast together with Prince Ande Xiong, Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Chong, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Gao Hui, General of the Right Guard Yu Qingze, and Area Commander of Wu Prefecture He Ruo Bi, and said, "In former days in the Zhou court I showed every mark of loyalty, yet I suffered constant suspicion and was chilled at heart time and again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor frequently had Lan dine with Prince Ande Xiong, Supreme Pillar of State Yuan Xie, Li Chong, Left Vice Director Gao Hui, General of the Right Guard Yu Qingze, and Wu Prefecture area commander He Ruo Bi, and said, "When I was still in the Zhou court I served with complete loyalty, yet I lived under endless suspicion and was repeatedly left heartsick.

sentences.zh: 為臣若此，竟何情賴？

translations.literal: If a subject is treated thus, upon what affection may he rely?
translations.idiomatic: What bond of trust can a minister have in such circumstances?

sentences.zh: 朕之於公，義則君臣，恩猶父子。

translations.literal: Between Us and you, the relation in duty is that of ruler and minister, but in affection it is like father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In my dealings with you, duty makes us sovereign and subject, yet in feeling we are as father and son.

sentences.zh: 朕當與公共用終吉，罪非謀逆，一無所問。

translations.literal: I shall share lasting good fortune with you; unless the crime is treason, I shall question you about nothing.
translations.idiomatic: I intend to share lasting prosperity with you; short of plotting rebellion, you need fear no inquiry from me.

sentences.zh: 朕亦知公至誠，特付太子，宜數參見之，庶得漸相親愛。

translations.literal: I also know your utmost sincerity and specially entrust you to the Crown Prince; you should visit him often, so that you may gradually grow close and fond of one another.
translations.idiomatic: I know your loyalty as well, and I am placing you especially in the service of the crown prince; visit him often so that affection may grow between you.

sentences.zh: 柱臣素望，實屬於公，宜識朕意。」

translations.literal: The pillar of the state and its long-standing hope truly rest upon you; you should understand My intent."
translations.idiomatic: The chief support of the realm and its enduring hope truly lie with you—bear my meaning in mind."

sentences.zh: 其恩禮如此。

translations.literal: His favor and courtesy were such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of favor and courtesy shown him.

sentences.zh: 又為蜀王秀納覽女為妃。

translations.literal: He also had Lan's daughter taken in marriage for Prince Xiu of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Lan's daughter marry Prince Xiu of Shu.

sentences.zh: 其後以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Later, on account of mourning for his mother, he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He later resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起令復位。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was ordered to resume his post.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 俄轉涇州刺史，所在並有政績。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Governor of Jing Prefecture; everywhere he served he left administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made governor of Jing Prefecture; in every post he won a record of good governance.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still holding office.

sentences.zh: 子洪嗣。

translations.literal: His son Hong succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hong inherited his line.

sentences.zh: 仕曆宋順臨三州刺史、司農少卿、北平太守。

translations.literal: In office he successively held the three prefectures of Song, Shun, and Lin, was Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries, and Governor of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hong served in turn as governor of Song, Shun, and Lin prefectures, as Vice Minister of the Imperial Granaries, and as governor of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 從子熾熾字仲光，上党文宣王稚之曾孫也。

translations.literal: His nephew Chi—Chi, courtesy name Zhongguang, was a great-grandson of Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang, Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Zhangsun Chi—Chi, whose courtesy name was Zhongguang, was a great-grandson of Prince Wenxuan of Shangdang, Zhi.

sentences.zh: 祖裕，魏太常卿、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu had been Director of the Imperial Sacrifices of Wei and Governor of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu had been the Northern Wei's Director of Imperial Sacrifices and governor of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父兕，周開府儀同三司、熊絳二州刺史、平原侯。

translations.literal: His father Si had been General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies of Zhou, Governor of the two prefectures of Xiong and Jiang, and Marquis of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Si had held the Northern Zhou rank of General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies, governed Xiong and Jiang prefectures, and been enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 熾性敏慧，美姿儀，頗涉群書，兼長武藝。

translations.literal: Chi was quick and clever by nature, handsome in bearing, had read widely among the various books, and was also skilled in martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was clever and perceptive by nature, striking in appearance, well read across many fields, and accomplished in the martial arts as well.

sentences.zh: 建德初，武帝尚道法，尤好玄言，求學兼經史、善於談論者，為通道館學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jiande era, Emperor Wu favored the Way and was especially fond of arcane discourse; he sought men learned in both classics and histories who were skilled in discussion, and appointed them scholars of the Hall of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiande era Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou favored Daoist teaching and especially loved abstruse discourse; he sought men versed in the classics and histories who could debate well and made them scholars of the Hall of the Way.

sentences.zh: 熾應其選，與英俊並遊，通涉彌博。

translations.literal: Chi answered the selection and associated with the outstanding talents, extending his knowledge ever more broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Chi was chosen for this company and moved among the finest minds of the day, broadening his learning still further.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，授雍州倉城令，尋轉盩啡令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande he was appointed Magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon transferred to be Magistrate of Dangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande 2 (573) he was appointed magistrate of Cangcheng in Yong Prefecture, and soon afterward was transferred to magistrate of Dangyin.

sentences.zh: 頻宰二邑，考績連最，遷崤郡守。

translations.literal: Having twice governed districts, his performance evaluations were repeatedly ranked highest; he was promoted to Administrator of Xiao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After governing two districts in succession with top evaluations, he was promoted to administrator of Xiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 入為禦正上士。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Senior Clerk of the Imperial Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court as Senior Clerk of the Imperial Censorate.

sentences.zh: 高祖作相，擢為丞相府功曹參軍，加大都督，封陽平縣子，邑二百戶。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor became Chancellor, Chi was promoted to Merit Officer in the Chancellor's office, given the additional rank of Grand Commander, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangping with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became Chancellor, Chi was raised to Merit Officer in the chancellor's office, given the additional rank of Grand Commander, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yangping with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 遷稍伯下大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Junior Grand Master of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Junior Grand Master of the Left.

sentences.zh: 其年王謙反，熾從信州總管王長述溯江而上。

translations.literal: That year Wang Qian rebelled; Chi followed Area Commander Wang Changshu up the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In that same year Wang Qian rose in rebellion; Chi accompanied Area Commander Wang Changshu up the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 以熾為前軍，破謙一鎮，定楚、合等五州，擒偽總管荊山西元振，以功拜儀同三司。

translations.literal: Chi was made vanguard, broke one of Qian's fortified posts, pacified the five prefectures of Chu, He, and others, captured the false area commander Yuan Zhen west of Jing Mountain, and for his merit was appointed General with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Chi served as vanguard, stormed one of Qian's strongpoints, pacified five prefectures including Chu and He, captured the rebel area commander Yuan Zhen west of Jing Mountain, and for this was made a general with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 及高祖受禪，熾率官屬先入清宮，即日授內史舍人、上儀同三司。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor received the abdication, Chi led the officials in first entering to secure the palace; that same day he was appointed Palace Scribe and Senior General with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian accepted the throne, Chi led the officials in first entering to secure the palace; that same day he was appointed Palace Scribe and Senior General with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官攝判東宮右庶子，出入兩宮，甚被委遇。

translations.literal: Soon, while retaining his original office, he was appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Eastern Palace and moved in and out of the two palaces, receiving great trust and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, while keeping his original post, he was made acting Right Vice Director of the crown prince's household and passed between the two palaces, enjoying deep trust.

sentences.zh: 加以處事周密，高祖每稱美之。

translations.literal: Moreover, because he handled affairs with thoroughness, the High Ancestor often praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he managed affairs with meticulous care, the emperor often spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 授左領軍長史，持節，使于東南道三十六州，廢置州郡，巡省風俗。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Left Guards, given credentials, and sent as commissioner to the thirty-six prefectures of the Southeast Circuit to abolish or establish prefectures and commanderies and to inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the Left Guards, given credentials, and dispatched as commissioner to thirty-six prefectures on the Southeast Circuit to reorganize prefectures and commanderies and inspect local customs.

sentences.zh: 還授太子僕，加諫議大夫，攝長安令。

translations.literal: On his return he was appointed Steward of the Crown Prince, given the additional title of Remonstrating Counselor, and appointed acting Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was appointed Steward of the Crown Prince, given the additional rank of Remonstrating Counselor, and made acting magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 與大興令梁毗俱為稱職。

translations.literal: Together with the Magistrate of Daxing, Liang Pi, he was equally regarded as fulfilling his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liang Pi, magistrate of Daxing, were both considered exemplary in office.

sentences.zh: 然毗以嚴正聞，熾以寬平顯，為政不同，部內各化。

translations.literal: Yet Pi was known for stern rectitude, while Chi was noted for lenient fairness; their styles of governance differed, yet each district was transformed under them.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was known for strict uprightness, Chi for mild fairness; though their methods differed, each brought order to his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 尋領右常平監，遷雍州贊治，改封饒良縣子。

translations.literal: Soon he took charge of the Right Ever-Normal Granary, was promoted to Assistant Administrator of Yong Prefecture, and his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Raoliang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he oversaw the Right Ever-Normal Granary, was promoted to assistant administrator of Yong Prefecture, and his title was changed to Viscount of Raoliang.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，轉太常少卿，進位開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Several years later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and advanced in rank to General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he became Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and was advanced to General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 複持節為河南道二十八州巡省大使，于路授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Again bearing credentials, he served as touring commissioner of the twenty-eight prefectures of the Henan Circuit, and on the road was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He again bore credentials as touring commissioner for twenty-eight prefectures on the Henan Circuit and, while on tour, was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，遷大理卿，複為西南道大使，巡省風俗。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye he was promoted to Director of the Court of Judicial Review, and again served as commissioner of the Southwest Circuit to inspect local customs.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 1 (605) he was made Director of the Court of Judicial Review and again sent as commissioner on the Southwest Circuit to inspect local customs.

sentences.zh: 擢拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾寇張掖，令熾率精騎五千擊走之，追至青海而還，以功授銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Tuyuhun raided Zhangye, Chi was ordered to lead five thousand picked horsemen to drive them off, pursued them to Qinghai, and returned; for his merit he was granted the title of Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tuyuhun attacked Zhangye, Chi was sent with five thousand elite cavalry to repulse them, pursued them to Qinghai, and returned; for this he received the title Silver-Gleaming Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 六年，幸江都宮，留熾于東都居守，仍攝左候衛將軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited the Jiangdu Palace, Chi was left at the Eastern Capital to hold the garrison and was also appointed acting commander of the Left Houwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the emperor traveled to the Jiangdu Palace, Chi was left at the Eastern Capital as commandant and also given acting command of the Left Houwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官，時年六十二。

translations.literal: That year he died in office, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office that same year, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 諡曰靜。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Jing ("Tranquil").

sentences.zh: 子安世，通事謁者。

translations.literal: His son Anshi was a Master of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi served as Master of Ceremonies for Receiving Guests.

sentences.zh: 熾弟晟晟字季晟，性通敏，略涉書記，善彈工射，趫捷過人。

translations.literal: Chi's younger brother Sheng—Sheng, courtesy name Jisheng, was penetrating and quick by nature, had a slight acquaintance with written records, was skilled at archery and mounted shooting, and was exceptionally agile.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's younger brother Zhangsun Sheng—Sheng, whose courtesy name was Jisheng, was quick-witted and responsive, knew something of clerical work, excelled at archery and mounted shooting, and was unusually nimble.

sentences.zh: 時周室尚武，貴遊子弟鹹以相矜，每共馳射，時輩皆出其下。

translations.literal: At that time the Zhou court valued martial prowess; the sons of the nobility all prided themselves on one another; whenever they rode and shot together, their contemporaries fell below him.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Zhou court then prized martial arts, and young men of noble families vied with one another; whenever they rode and shot together, none of his peers could match him.

sentences.zh: 年十八，為司衛上士。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was a Senior Clerk in the Ministry of Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he was a senior clerk in the Ministry of Guards.

sentences.zh: 初未知名，人弗之識也，唯高祖一見，深嗟異焉，乃攜其手而謂人曰：「長孫郎武藝逸群，適與其言，又多奇略。

translations.literal: At first he was not yet known, and people did not recognize his worth; only the High Ancestor, upon a single meeting, sighed deeply in wonder at him, took his hand, and said to those present, "Young Master Zhangsun's martial skill stands above the crowd; suited to his words, he also has many extraordinary stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was unknown and no one took notice of him, but the High Ancestor, on meeting him once, was struck with wonder, took his hand, and said to those present, "This young Zhangsun's martial prowess is beyond the common run; to judge by his speech he also holds many remarkable stratagems.

sentences.zh: 後之名將，非此子邪？」

translations.literal: The famous general of later times—is it not this man?"
translations.idiomatic: The great commander of a later day—will it not be he?"

sentences.zh: 宣帝時，突厥攝圖請婚于周，以趙王招女妻之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan, the Türk qaghan Shetu requested marriage with Zhou; the daughter of Prince Zhao of Zhao was given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuan, the Türk qaghan Shetu sought a marriage alliance with Zhou, and Prince Zhao's daughter was given to him as wife.

sentences.zh: 然周與攝圖各相誇競，妙選驍勇以充使者，因遣晟副汝南公宇文神慶送千金公主至其牙。

translations.literal: Yet Zhou and Shetu each strove to outdo the other, choosing the fiercest warriors to serve as envoys; Sheng was therefore sent as deputy to the Duke of Runan, Yuwen Shenqing, to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to the qaghan's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou and Shetu each tried to outshine the other by selecting the boldest warriors as envoys, and Sheng was sent as deputy to the Duke of Runan, Yuwen Shenqing, to escort the Princess of a Thousand Gold to the qaghan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 前後使人數十輩，攝圖多不禮，見晟而獨愛焉，每共遊獵，留之竟歲。

translations.literal: Envoys before and after numbered several tens; Shetu was discourteous to most of them, but when he saw Sheng he alone took a liking to him, hunted with him constantly, and kept him for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of envoys had come before and after, and Shetu had treated most of them with little courtesy, but he took a special liking to Sheng, hunted with him constantly, and kept him for an entire year.

sentences.zh: 嘗有二雕，飛而爭肉，因以兩箭與晟曰：「請射取之。」

translations.literal: Once there were two hawks flying and fighting over meat; he therefore gave Sheng two arrows and said, "Please shoot and take them."
translations.idiomatic: Once two hawks were fighting in the air over a piece of meat; Shetu handed Sheng two arrows and said, "Shoot them down for me."

sentences.zh: 晟乃彎弓馳往，遇雕相攫，遂一發而雙貫焉。

translations.literal: Sheng then bent his bow and galloped forward; when he met the hawks grappling together, with one shot he pierced them both.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng bent his bow, spurred forward, found the birds locked together, and brought down both with a single arrow.

sentences.zh: 攝圖喜，命諸子弟貴人皆相親友，冀昵近之，以學彈射。

translations.literal: Shetu was pleased and ordered all his younger brothers, sons, and nobles to befriend him, hoping to draw near him and learn archery.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, Shetu had his younger kinsmen and nobles befriend Sheng so that they might stay close to him and learn his archery.

sentences.zh: 其弟處羅侯號突利設，尤得眾心。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chuluohou, titled Tuli she, was especially beloved by the people.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chuluohou, who bore the title Tuli she, enjoyed exceptional popularity.

sentences.zh: 而為攝圖所忌，密托心腹，陰與晟盟。

translations.literal: Yet he was envied by Shetu; he secretly entrusted his heart to trusted men and made a secret alliance with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu envied him, however; Chuluohou secretly placed his trust in confidants and entered a covert alliance with Sheng.

sentences.zh: 晟與之遊獵，因察山川形勢，部眾強弱，皆盡知之。

translations.literal: When Sheng hunted with him, he thereby observed the lay of mountains and rivers, the strength and weakness of the tribes—he came to know them all thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: On their hunting expeditions Sheng surveyed the terrain, the strength of the tribes, and their dispositions until he knew them through and through.

sentences.zh: 時高祖作相，晟以狀白高祖。

translations.literal: At that time the High Ancestor was Chancellor; Sheng reported the situation to the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian was then Chancellor; Sheng laid out what he had learned before him.

sentences.zh: 高祖大喜，遷奉車都尉。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor was greatly pleased and promoted him to Master of the Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor was delighted and promoted him to Master of the Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 至開皇元年，攝圖曰：「我周家親也，今隋公自立而不能制，複何面目見可賀敦乎」？

translations.literal: By the first year of Kaihuang, Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou; now the Duke of Sui has set himself up and I cannot restrain him—what face have I to show the qaghan?"
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 1 (581) Shetu said, "I am kin to the house of Zhou, yet now the Duke of Sui has seized power and I cannot stop him—how can I face the qaghan?"

sentences.zh: 因與高寶寧攻陷臨渝鎮，約諸面部落謀共南侵。

translations.literal: He therefore joined Gao Baoning in attacking and capturing Lin Prefecture's Yu Pass, and arranged with the various tribal chiefs to plot a joint invasion southward.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Gao Baoning in storming Lin Prefecture's Yu Pass and conspired with the tribal chiefs of the various departments for a joint southern invasion.

sentences.zh: 高祖新立，由是大懼，修築長城，發兵屯北境，命陰壽鎮幽州，虞慶則鎮并州，屯兵數萬人以為之備。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor had only lately taken the throne and was therefore greatly alarmed; he repaired the Long Wall, sent troops to garrison the northern frontier, ordered Yin Shou to hold You Prefecture and Yu Qingze to hold Bing Prefecture, and stationed tens of thousands of men as a precaution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had only just ascended the throne and was deeply alarmed; he repaired the Great Wall, posted troops along the northern border, placed Yin Shou at You Prefecture and Yu Qingze at Bing Prefecture, and stationed tens of thousands of men in readiness.

sentences.zh: 晟先知攝圖、玷厥、阿波、突利等叔侄兄弟各統強兵，俱號可汗，分居四面，內懷猜忌，外示和同，難以力征，易可離間，因上書曰：「臣聞喪亂之極，必致升平，是故上天啟其機，聖人成其務。

translations.literal: Sheng had already known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and others—these uncles, nephews, and brothers—each commanded strong armies, all styled themselves qaghan, and held separate domains on four sides; inwardly they harbored suspicion, outwardly they showed harmony; they could not easily be overcome by force, but might readily be set at odds; he therefore submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant has heard that the extreme of disorder must lead to great peace; therefore Heaven opens the opportunity and the sage completes the task.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng had long known that Shetu, Dianjue, Abo, Tuli, and other kinsmen each commanded powerful forces, all called themselves qaghan, and held separate domains on four sides; inwardly suspicious yet outwardly cordial, they could not easily be crushed by force but could readily be divided; he therefore memorialized, "I have heard that the depth of disorder must give way to great peace, and that Heaven opens the moment for the sage to complete the work.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下當百王之末，膺千載之期，諸夏雖安，戎場尚梗，興師致討，未是其時，棄於度外，又複侵擾。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty the Emperor, at the end of the hundred kings, has received the charge of a thousand-year age; though the various Xia are at peace, the frontier of the Rong is still obstructed; to raise armies and launch punitive expeditions is not yet the time, yet to cast them beyond concern is again to invite their raids.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty stands at the close of a long line of kings and has received the mandate of a new age; though the heartland is settled, the northern frontier remains troubled; to march in force is not yet timely, yet to ignore the tribes is only to invite fresh raids.

sentences.zh: 故宜密運籌策，漸以攘之，計失則百姓不甯，計得則萬代之福。

translations.literal: Therefore secret stratagems should be employed, gradually to displace them; if the plan fails, the common people will know no peace; if the plan succeeds, it will be the blessing of ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Secret strategy should therefore be applied to wear them down step by step; failure would leave the people unquiet, success would secure the welfare of generations to come.

sentences.zh: 吉凶所系，伏願詳思。

translations.literal: Fortune and misfortune depend upon this; I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Upon this good or ill fortune turns; I beg Your Majesty to weigh it with care.

sentences.zh: 臣於週末，忝充外使，匈奴倚伏，實所具知。

translations.literal: Your servant, at the end of Zhou, was privileged to serve as envoy abroad; the rises and falls of the Xiongnu I know in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Zhou dynasty I had the honor of serving abroad as envoy and came to know the Türks' strengths and weaknesses in detail.

sentences.zh: 玷厥之於攝圖，兵強而位下，外名相屬，內隙已彰，鼓動其情，必將自戰。

translations.literal: Dianjue toward Shetu has strong troops but a lower position; outwardly they are joined in name, but inwardly the rift is already clear; if their passions are stirred, they will surely fight one another.
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue stands to Shetu with strong forces but inferior rank; though linked in name, the breach within is already plain, and if their passions are provoked they will turn on each other.

sentences.zh: 又處羅侯者，攝圖之弟，奸多而勢弱，曲取於眾心，國人愛之，因為攝圖所忌，其心殊不自安，跡示彌縫，實懷疑懼。

translations.literal: Again Chuluohou is Shetu's younger brother—cunning and many in followers yet weak in power; he curries favor with the people's hearts and is therefore envied by Shetu; his heart is especially ill at ease; outwardly he shows conciliation, but inwardly he is full of doubt and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou, Shetu's younger brother, is crafty and popular yet militarily weak; beloved by the tribes, he is envied by Shetu, lives in deep unease, and though he appears accommodating is inwardly fearful.

sentences.zh: 又阿波首鼠，介在其間，頗畏攝圖，受其牽率，唯強是與，未有定心。

translations.literal: Again Abo is irresolute, standing between them; he fears Shetu somewhat and is dragged along by him, following only the strong and having no settled mind.
translations.idiomatic: Abo, caught between them, is timid and irresolute, somewhat afraid of Shetu and pulled along in his wake, siding with whoever is stronger and never firm in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 今宜遠交而近攻，離強而合弱，通使玷厥，說合阿波，則攝圖回兵，自防右地。

translations.literal: Now one should befriend those far and attack those near, divide the strong and unite the weak, send envoys to Dianjue and win Abo over—then Shetu will turn his army back to guard his western domain.
translations.idiomatic: The policy now should be to ally with those far off and strike those near, to separate the strong and unite the weak: send envoys to Dianjue and draw Abo to our side, and Shetu will have to wheel his army back to defend the west.

sentences.zh: 又引處羅，遣連奚、霫，則攝圖分眾，還備左方。

translations.literal: Again draw in Chuluohou and link him with the Xi and Mohe—then Shetu will divide his forces and return to guard the left.
translations.idiomatic: Win over Chuluohou and connect him with the Xi and Mohe as well, and Shetu will have to split his forces to guard the east.

sentences.zh: 首尾猜嫌，腹心離阻，十數年後，承釁討之，必可一舉而空其國矣。」

translations.literal: With suspicion at head and tail and division at the center, after ten-odd years, when an opportunity arises to strike, one may surely in a single campaign empty their state."
translations.idiomatic: Caught between mutual suspicion and a divided heart, within a dozen years or so, when occasion offers, a single campaign should suffice to destroy their power entirely."

sentences.zh: 上省表大悅，因召與語。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial with great delight and summoned him to speak.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with great delight and summoned him for a private audience.

sentences.zh: 晟複口陳形勢，手畫山川，寫其虛實，皆如指掌。

translations.literal: Sheng again set forth the situation orally, drew mountains and rivers with his hand, and wrote out their strengths and weaknesses—all as clear as the palm of his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng again described the situation in person, sketched the mountains and rivers, and laid out their strengths and weaknesses with the clarity of a map in his palm.

sentences.zh: 上深嗟異，皆納用焉。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed deeply in wonder and adopted all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and adopted every point.

sentences.zh: 因遣太僕元暉出伊吾道，使詣玷厥，賜以狼頭纛，謬為欽敬，禮數甚優。

translations.literal: He therefore sent the Master of the Imperial Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu road as envoy to Dianjue, presenting a wolf-head banner and feigning deep respect, with ceremonial honors very generous.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore dispatched the Master of the Imperial Stud Yuan Hui by the Yiwu route to Dianjue, presenting a wolf-head banner and treating him with exaggerated respect and lavish ceremony.

sentences.zh: 玷厥使來，引居攝圖使上。

translations.literal: When Dianjue's envoy came, he was given precedence above Shetu's envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Dianjue's envoy arrived, he was seated above Shetu's envoy.

sentences.zh: 反間既行，果相猜貳。

translations.literal: Once the stratagem of alienation was set in motion, they indeed came to suspect and divide one another.
translations.idiomatic: Once the policy of sowing discord took effect, the Türks indeed turned suspicious and divided among themselves.

sentences.zh: 授晟車騎將軍，出黃龍道，齎幣賜奚、霫、契丹等，遣為嚮導，得至處羅侯所，深布心腹，誘令內附。

translations.literal: Sheng was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, went out by the Yellow Dragon road, carried gifts to bestow upon the Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and others, and sent them as guides so that he reached Chuluohou's camp, laid his heart bare in depth, and induced him to submit inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was made General of Chariots and Cavalry, marched out by the Yellow Dragon route, presented gifts to the Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and others, and used them as guides until he reached Chuluohou, won his confidence, and persuaded him to submit to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 二年，攝圖四十萬騎自蘭州入，至於周盤，破達奚長儒軍，更欲南入。

translations.literal: In the second year, Shetu with four hundred thousand horsemen entered from Lan Prefecture as far as Zhoupan, defeated the army of the Chief of the West, Daxi Changru, and wished to press farther south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Shetu led four hundred thousand horsemen in from Lan Prefecture to Zhoupan, routed Chief of the West Daxi Changru's army, and prepared to drive farther south.

sentences.zh: 玷厥不從，引兵而去。

translations.literal: Dianjue would not follow and led his troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue refused to join him and withdrew with his forces.

sentences.zh: 時晟又說染幹詐告攝圖曰：「鐵勒等反，欲襲其牙。」

translations.literal: At that time Sheng also persuaded Rangan to feign a report to Shetu, saying, "The Tiele and others have rebelled and intend to strike your headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng also had Rangan send a false report to Shetu: "The Tiele tribes have risen and mean to attack your headquarters."

sentences.zh: 攝圖乃懼，回兵出塞。

translations.literal: Shetu thereupon grew afraid and turned his army back beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Shetu wheeled his army back beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 後數月，突厥大入，發八道元帥分出拒之。

translations.literal: Several months later the Türks invaded on a great scale; eight campaigning commanders-in-chief were dispatched on separate routes to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Some months later the Türks raided in force, and eight campaigning commanders-in-chief were sent out on separate routes to meet them.

sentences.zh: 阿波至涼州，與竇榮定戰，賊帥累北。

translations.literal: Abo reached Liang Prefecture and fought Dou Rongding; the enemy commander was repeatedly driven north.
translations.idiomatic: Abo reached Liang Prefecture and fought Dou Rongding; the Türk leader was beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 時晟為偏將，使謂之曰：「攝圖每來，戰皆大勝。

translations.literal: At that time Sheng was a subordinate commander and sent someone to say to him, "Whenever Shetu comes, his battles are all great victories.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, then a subordinate commander, sent word to Abo: "Whenever Shetu takes the field he wins a great victory.

sentences.zh: 阿波才入，便即致敗，此乃突厥之恥，豈不內愧於心乎？

translations.literal: Abo has only just entered and already suffers defeat—this is a disgrace to the Türks; will you not feel shame inwardly?
translations.idiomatic: You have scarcely crossed the border and already been defeated—is this not a shame to all the Türks? Can you not feel the sting of it?

sentences.zh: 且攝圖之與阿波，兵勢本敵。

translations.literal: Moreover, between Shetu and Abo their military strength was originally equal.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Shetu and Abo were once evenly matched in strength.

sentences.zh: 今攝圖日勝，為眾所崇，阿波不利，為國生辱。

translations.literal: Now Shetu wins day by day and is honored by the masses, while Abo fares ill and brings disgrace upon the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now Shetu wins victory after victory and rises in the people's esteem, while your setbacks bring dishonor on the realm.

sentences.zh: 攝圖必當因以罪歸於阿波，成其夙計，滅北牙矣。

translations.literal: Shetu will surely therefore lay the blame upon Abo and accomplish his long-standing design to destroy the Northern Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu will surely use this to blame you and carry out his old plan to destroy the Northern Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 願自量度，能禦之乎？」

translations.literal: Consider for yourself whether you can withstand him."
translations.idiomatic: Measure your own strength—can you stand against him?"

sentences.zh: 阿波使至，晟又謂之曰：「今達頭與隋連和，而攝圖不能制。

translations.literal: When Abo's envoy arrived, Sheng again said to him, "Now Datou is allied with Sui, yet Shetu cannot control him.
translations.idiomatic: When Abo's envoy came, Sheng told him further, "Datou is now allied with Sui, yet Shetu cannot restrain him.

sentences.zh: 可汗何不依附天子，連結達頭，相合為強，此萬全之計。

translations.literal: Why does the qaghan not attach himself to the Son of Heaven and join with Datou? United you would be strong—this is a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: Why not submit to the Son of Heaven and join with Datou? Together you would be formidable—this is the sure course.

sentences.zh: 豈若喪兵負罪，歸就攝圖，受其戮辱邪？」

translations.literal: How is it better to lose troops, bear guilt, and return to Shetu to suffer slaughter and humiliation?"
translations.idiomatic: Is it wiser to lose your army, bear disgrace, and return to Shetu only to be killed and shamed?"

sentences.zh: 阿波納之，因留塞上，使人隨晟入朝。

translations.literal: Abo accepted this and therefore remained on the frontier, sending men to follow Sheng into court.
translations.idiomatic: Abo agreed, stayed on the border, and sent envoys to accompany Sheng to court.

sentences.zh: 時攝圖與衛王軍遇，戰于白道，敗走至磧。

translations.literal: At that time Shetu encountered the army of Prince Wei and fought at Baidao; defeated, he fled to the desert.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu then met Prince Wei's army at Baidao, was defeated, and fled into the desert.

sentences.zh: 聞阿波懷貳，乃掩北牙，盡獲其眾而殺其母。

translations.literal: Hearing that Abo harbored disloyalty, he suddenly struck the Northern Headquarters, seized all his followers, and killed his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Abo was disloyal, he suddenly attacked the Northern Headquarters, seized Abo's followers, and killed Abo's mother.

sentences.zh: 阿波還無所歸，西奔玷厥，乞師十余萬，東擊攝圖，複得故地，收散卒數萬，與攝圖相攻。

translations.literal: Abo returned with nowhere to go, fled west to Dianjue, and begged more than a hundred thousand troops; marching east he attacked Shetu, recovered his old territory, gathered several tens of thousands of scattered soldiers, and fought Shetu.
translations.idiomatic: Abo, with nowhere to turn, fled west to Dianjue and borrowed more than a hundred thousand men; marching east he struck Shetu, recovered his old lands, rallied tens of thousands of scattered troops, and fought him again.

sentences.zh: 阿波頻勝，其勢益張。

translations.literal: Abo won repeatedly and his power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Abo won battle after battle and his power swelled.

sentences.zh: 攝圖又遣使朝貢，公主自請改姓，乞為帝女，上許之。

translations.literal: Shetu again sent envoys with tribute to court; the princess herself asked to change her surname, begging to become the emperor's daughter, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu again sent tribute to court; the princess asked to take the imperial surname and be adopted as the emperor's daughter, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 四年，遣晟副虞慶則使於攝圖，賜公主姓為楊氏，改封大義公主。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Sheng was sent as deputy to Yu Qingze on a mission to Shetu, granting the princess the surname Yang and changing her enfeoffment to Princess Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Sheng accompanied Yu Qingze to Shetu's camp, gave the princess the surname Yang, and enfeoffed her as Princess Dayi.

sentences.zh: 攝圖奉詔，不肯起拜，晟進曰：「突厥與隋俱是大國天子，可汗不起，安敢違意。

translations.literal: Shetu received the edict but refused to rise and bow; Sheng advanced and said, "Türks and Sui are alike great states of the Son of Heaven; if the qaghan does not rise, how dare we go against his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Shetu received the edict but would not rise to bow. Sheng stepped forward and said, "Türks and Sui are both great powers under Heaven; if the qaghan will not rise, we dare not press him.

sentences.zh: 但可賀敦為帝女，則可汗是大隋女婿，奈何無禮，不敬婦公乎？」

translations.literal: Yet Kehedun is the emperor's daughter; then the qaghan is the Great Sui's son-in-law—how can you be without courtesy and fail to respect your wife's father?"
translations.idiomatic: But Kehedun is the emperor's daughter, which makes you the Great Sui's son-in-law—how can you be so rude as not to honor your father-in-law?"

sentences.zh: 攝圖乃笑謂其達官曰：「須拜婦公，我從之耳。」

translations.literal: Shetu then laughed and said to his high officials, "I must bow to my father-in-law; I shall follow this."
translations.idiomatic: Shetu laughed and told his nobles, "I must bow to my father-in-law—I will do as he says."

sentences.zh: 於是乃拜詔書。

translations.literal: Thereupon he bowed to the edict.
translations.idiomatic: With that he bowed to the edict.

sentences.zh: 使還稱旨，授儀同三司、左勳衛車騎將軍。

translations.literal: When the mission returned and reported that it had fulfilled its charge, Sheng was appointed General with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies and General of Chariots and Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On their return, with the mission deemed successful, Sheng was appointed a general with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies and General of Chariots and Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard.

sentences.zh: 七年，攝圖死，遣晟持節拜其弟處羅侯為莫何可汗，以其子雍閭為葉護可汗。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was sent bearing credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Qaghan Mohe and his son Yonglu as Yabghu Qaghan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shetu died; Sheng was dispatched with credentials to invest his younger brother Chuluohou as Qaghan Mohe and his son Yonglu as Yabghu Qaghan.

sentences.zh: 處羅侯因晟奏曰：「阿波為天所滅，與五六千騎在山谷間，伏聽詔旨，當取之以獻。」

translations.literal: Chuluohou thereupon memorialized through Sheng, "Abo has been destroyed by Heaven and remains in a valley with five or six thousand horsemen, awaiting the imperial command; I shall take him and present him as captive."
translations.idiomatic: Chuluohou reported through Sheng, "Abo has been brought low by Heaven and lingers in the valleys with five or six thousand horsemen, waiting on your command; I will seize him and present him as captive."

sentences.zh: 乃召文武議焉。

translations.literal: The emperor then summoned the civil and military officials to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The court then debated the matter.

sentences.zh: 樂安西元諧曰：「請就彼梟首，以懲其惡。」

translations.literal: Yuan Xie of Le'an in the west said, "Let them behead him on the spot to punish his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xie of Le'an said, "Let them behead him where he stands to punish his crimes.

sentences.zh: 武陽公李充曰：「請生將入朝，顯戮以示百姓。」

translations.literal: Li Chong, Duke of Wuyang, said, "Let him be brought alive to court and displayed in execution before the people."
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Duke of Wuyang, said, "Bring him alive to the capital and execute him publicly as an example."

sentences.zh: 上謂晟曰：「於卿何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked Sheng, "What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Sheng, "What is your view?"

sentences.zh: 晟對曰：「若突厥背誕，須齊之以刑。

translations.literal: Sheng replied, "If the Türks turn treacherous, they must be restrained by punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng answered, "If the Türks were openly rebellious, punishment would be fitting.

sentences.zh: 今其昆弟自相夷滅，阿波之惡，非負國家，因其困窮，取而為戮，恐非招遠之道，不如兩存之。」

translations.literal: Now their brothers destroy one another; Abo's offense is not a crime against the state. To seize him in his distress and put him to death would, I fear, not be the way to draw the distant near; it would be better to preserve both."
translations.idiomatic: But now they are destroying one another. Abo's wrong was not against our state; to kill him in his extremity would not win the distant tribes. Better to let both survive."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 八年，處羅侯死，遣晟往吊，仍齎陳國所獻寶器以賜雍閭。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to offer condolences and also carried the precious objects presented by Chen to bestow upon Yonglu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Chuluohou died; Sheng was sent to mourn him and carried treasures that Chen had presented to bestow upon Yonglu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，流人楊欽亡入突厥，詐言彭公劉昶共宇文氏女謀欲反隋，稱遣其來，密告主。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the exile Yang Qin fled into the Türk lands and falsely claimed that Duke Peng Liu Chang, together with a daughter of the house of Yuwen, plotted rebellion against Sui, saying he had been sent to report this secretly to their lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the exile Yang Qin fled to the Türks and falsely claimed that Duke Peng Liu Chang and a daughter of the Yuwen house were plotting to rebel against Sui and that he had been sent to inform them in secret.

sentences.zh: 雍閭信之，乃不修職貢。

translations.literal: Yonglu believed this and therefore ceased presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu believed him and stopped sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 又遣晟出使，微觀察焉。

translations.literal: Sheng was again sent on mission to observe him closely.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was again sent as envoy to observe him closely.

sentences.zh: 公主見晟，乃言辭不遜，又遣所私胡人安遂迦共欽計議，扇惑雍閭。

translations.literal: When the princess saw Sheng, her words were insolent; she also sent her private Türk follower Ansuijia to plot with Qin and incite Yonglu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess received Sheng with insolent speech and sent her private agent, the Hu man Ansuijia, to conspire with Qin and stir Yonglu to revolt.

sentences.zh: 晟至京師，具以狀奏。

translations.literal: When Sheng reached the capital he memorialized the full account.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital Sheng laid the whole matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 又遣晟往索欽，雍閭欲勿與，謬答曰：「檢校客內，無此色人。」

translations.literal: He was again sent to demand Qin; Yonglu wished not to surrender him and answered falsely, "We have searched among the guests and there is no man of that description."
translations.idiomatic: He was sent again to demand Qin; Yonglu tried to withhold him and answered falsely, "We have searched our guests and found no such person."

sentences.zh: 晟乃貨其達官，知欽所在，夜掩獲之，以示雍閭，因發公主私事，國人大恥。

translations.literal: Sheng then bribed his high officials, learned where Qin was, seized him by a night raid, showed him to Yonglu, and thereby exposed the princess's private conduct; the Türk people were deeply shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng bribed Yonglu's nobles, learned Qin's whereabouts, seized him in a night raid, and showed him to Yonglu, exposing the princess's misconduct and shaming the nation.

sentences.zh: 雍閭執遂迦等，並以付晟。

translations.literal: Yonglu seized Ansuijia and the others and handed them all over to Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu arrested Ansuijia and the rest and delivered them to Sheng.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，加授開府，仍遣入籓，蒞殺大義公主。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, gave him the additional rank of General-in-Chief, and again sent him into the Türk domain to go and execute Princess Dayi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, promoted him to General-in-Chief, and sent him back into the Türk lands to execute Princess Dayi.

sentences.zh: 雍閭又表請婚，僉議將許之。

translations.literal: Yonglu again petitioned requesting marriage; the assembled officials deliberated and were about to consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu again petitioned for a marriage alliance, and the court was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 晟又奏曰：「臣觀雍閭，反覆無信，特共玷厥有隙，所以依倚國家。

translations.literal: Sheng again memorialized, "Your servant observes that Yonglu is faithless and inconstant; he relies on the state only because he happens to be at odds with Dianjue.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized again, "Yonglu is fickle and untrustworthy; he clings to us only because he is at odds with Dianjue.

sentences.zh: 縱與為婚，終當必叛。

translations.literal: Even if a marriage is granted, in the end he will surely rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him a princess and he will rebel in the end.

sentences.zh: 今若得尚公主，承藉威靈，玷厥、染幹必又受其徵發。

translations.literal: If he now obtains an imperial princess and borrows her prestige, Dianjue and Rangan will surely again suffer his requisitions.
translations.idiomatic: Once he has an imperial princess and borrows her prestige, Dianjue and Rangan will again be subject to his demands.

sentences.zh: 強而更反，後恐難圖。

translations.literal: When he grows strong he will turn against us again; he will then be hard to deal with.
translations.idiomatic: When he grows strong he will turn on us again, and then he will be hard to control.

sentences.zh: 且染幹者，處羅侯之子也，素有誠款，於今兩代。

translations.literal: Moreover Rangan is the son of Chuluohou and has long shown sincere loyalty through two generations.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan, the son of Chuluohou, has shown sincere loyalty across two reigns.

sentences.zh: 臣前與相見，亦乞通婚，不如許之，招令南徙，兵少力弱，易可撫馴，使敵雍閭，以為邊捍。」

translations.literal: When I met him before he too asked for marriage; it would be better to grant this, induce him to move south, and since his troops are few and his power weak he can easily be pacified and made to oppose Yonglu as a frontier shield."
translations.idiomatic: He too once asked for a marriage when I met him; better to grant it, move him south, and since his forces are few and weak, pacify him easily and set him against Yonglu as a border shield."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Agreed."

sentences.zh: 又遣慰喻染幹，許尚公主。

translations.literal: He again sent envoys to comfort Rangan and promised him an imperial princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to reassure Rangan and promised him an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 十七年，染幹遣五百騎隨晟來逆女，以宗女封安義公主以妻之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Rangan sent five hundred horsemen with Sheng to escort the bride; an imperial clanswoman was enfeoffed as Princess Anyi and given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Rangan sent five hundred horsemen with Sheng to fetch his bride; a clanswoman was enfeoffed as Princess Anyi and given to him.

sentences.zh: 晟說染幹率眾南徙，居度斤舊鎮。

translations.literal: Sheng persuaded Rangan to lead his people south and settle them at the old headquarters of Dujin.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng persuaded Rangan to move his people south to the old site at Dujin.

sentences.zh: 雍閭疾之，亟來抄略。

translations.literal: Yonglu resented this and repeatedly came to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Yonglu resented this and raided again and again.

sentences.zh: 染幹伺知動靜，輒遣奏聞，是以賊來每先有備。

translations.literal: Rangan, whenever he learned of movements, at once sent word to court; therefore whenever the enemy came there was always prior warning.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan reported every movement to court, so the frontier was forewarned whenever Yonglu struck.

sentences.zh: 十九年，染幹因晟奏，雍閭作攻具，欲打大同城。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, through Sheng's memorial, Rangan reported that Yonglu was making siege engines and intended to attack Datong city.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Rangan reported through Sheng that Yonglu was building siege engines to attack Datong.

sentences.zh: 詔發六總管，並取漢王節度，分道出塞討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered six area commanders, all under the command of Prince Han, to march out of the frontier on separate routes to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered six area commanders, all under Prince Han, to march beyond the border on separate routes against him.

sentences.zh: 雍閭大懼，複共達頭同盟，合力掩襲染幹，大戰于長城下。

translations.literal: Yonglu was greatly alarmed and again allied with Datou; together they launched a surprise attack on Rangan and fought a great battle below the Great Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Yonglu allied again with Datou; together they fell on Rangan in a great battle below the Great Wall.

sentences.zh: 染幹敗績，殺其兄弟子侄，而部落亡散。

translations.literal: Rangan was defeated; his brothers, sons, and nephews were killed, and his tribes scattered and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan was routed; his brothers, sons, and nephews were killed and his tribes scattered.

sentences.zh: 染幹與晟獨以五騎逼夜南走，至旦，行百餘裡，收得數百騎，乃相與謀曰：「今兵敗入朝，一降人耳，大隋天子豈禮我乎？

translations.literal: Rangan and Sheng alone, with five horsemen, fled south through the night; by dawn they had gone more than a hundred li, gathered several hundred horsemen, and then deliberated together, "Now that our army is defeated, if we enter court we are merely surrendered men—will the Son of Heaven of Great Sui treat us with courtesy?
translations.idiomatic: Rangan and Sheng fled south with only five horsemen; by dawn, after more than a hundred li, they had gathered a few hundred riders and said to one another, "Defeated, if we submit we are mere captives—will the Son of Heaven honor us?

sentences.zh: 玷厥雖來，本無冤隙，若往投之，必相存濟。」

translations.literal: Though Dianjue is coming, we originally had no grievance with him; if we go over to him he will surely preserve us."
translations.idiomatic: Dianjue is near and we have no old quarrel with him; if we go to him he will surely shelter us."

sentences.zh: 晟知其懷貳，乃密遣從者入伏遠鎮，令速舉烽。

translations.literal: Sheng knew his mind was divided and secretly sent a follower into Fuyuan Fort to order beacon fires raised at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng saw his wavering and secretly sent a man into Fuyuan Fort to have the beacon fires lit immediately.

sentences.zh: 染幹見四烽俱發，問晟曰：「城上然烽何也？」

translations.literal: When Rangan saw four beacon fires all raised, he asked Sheng, "Why are beacon fires lit on the wall?"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing four beacons ablaze, Rangan asked Sheng, "Why are the beacon towers burning?"

sentences.zh: 晟紿之曰：「城高地迥，必遙見賊來。

translations.literal: Sheng deceived him, saying, "The city is high and the land stretches far; they must see the enemy coming from afar.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng answered, "The walls are high and the plain wide—they must see the enemy from far off.

sentences.zh: 我國家法，若賊少舉二烽，來多舉三烽，大逼舉四烽，使見賊多而又近耳。」

translations.literal: By our state's law, if the enemy are few they raise two beacons, if many they raise three, and if the pressure is great they raise four—so that one sees the enemy are many and near."
translations.idiomatic: Our law is: few enemies, two fires; many enemies, three; great force, four—so you see they are numerous and close."

sentences.zh: 染幹大懼，謂其眾曰：「追兵已逼，且可投城。」

translations.literal: Rangan was greatly afraid and said to his followers, "Pursuers are already near; for the present let us enter the fort."
translations.idiomatic: Rangan was terrified and told his men, "The pursuers are upon us—we must take refuge in the fort."

sentences.zh: 既入鎮，晟留其達官執室以領其眾，自將染幹馳驛入朝。

translations.literal: Once inside the fort, Sheng detained his high official Zhishi to command the masses, while he himself led Rangan by post-horse into court.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the fort Sheng left Rangan's noble Zhishi in command of the troops and himself escorted Rangan by relay horse to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，進授左勳衛驃騎將軍，持節護突厥。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted him to General of Agile Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard, gave him credentials, and appointed him protector of the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was overjoyed, promoted Sheng to General of Agile Cavalry of the Left Merit Guard, gave him credentials, and made him protector of the Türks.

sentences.zh: 晟遣降虜覘候雍閭，知其牙內屢有災變，夜見赤虹，光照數百里，天狗隕，雨血三日，流星墜其營內，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Sheng sent surrendered Türks to spy on Yonglu and learned that within his headquarters there were repeated portents: by night a red rainbow shone, its light covering several hundred li; a heaven-dog fell; blood rained for three days; a meteor struck his camp with a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent surrendered Türks to watch Yonglu and learned that his camp was plagued by omens—a red rainbow lighting the sky for hundreds of li, a heaven-dog falling, three days of bloody rain, a meteor crashing into his camp with thunder.

sentences.zh: 每夜自驚，言隋師且至。

translations.literal: Each night he startled himself, saying the Sui army was about to come.
translations.idiomatic: Each night he woke in alarm, saying the Sui army was coming.

sentences.zh: 並遣奏知，仍請出討突厥。

translations.literal: Sheng reported all this and again asked permission to march out against the Türks.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng reported everything and again asked leave to campaign against the Türks.

sentences.zh: 都速等歸染幹，前後至者男女萬餘口，晟安置之。

translations.literal: Dusu and others returned to Rangan; men and women numbering more than ten thousand came before and after, and Sheng settled them.
translations.idiomatic: Dusu and others returned to Rangan; more than ten thousand men and women came in succession, and Sheng settled them.

sentences.zh: 由是突厥悅附。

translations.literal: Thereby the Türks were pleased and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: From this the Türks were won to willing submission.

sentences.zh: 尋以染幹為意利珍豆啟人可汗，賜射于武安殿。

translations.literal: Before long Rangan was appointed Qaghan Yili Zhen Douqi and granted an archery contest in the Hall of Martial Peace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Rangan was invested as Qaghan Yili Zhen Douqi and given an archery contest in the Hall of Martial Peace.

sentences.zh: 選善射者十二人，分為兩朋。

translations.literal: Twelve skilled archers were chosen and divided into two sides.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve skilled archers were chosen and divided into two teams.

sentences.zh: 啟人曰：「臣由長孫大使得見天子，今日賜射，願入其朋。」

translations.literal: The qaghan said, "Through the Great Master Zhangsun I have seen the Son of Heaven; today, granted this shooting match, I wish to enter his side."
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan said, "Through Master Zhangsun I have seen the Son of Heaven; grant me a place on his team in today's contest."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: This was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Permission was given.

sentences.zh: 給晟箭六侯，發皆入鹿，啟人之朋竟勝。

translations.literal: Sheng was given six targets; every shot entered the deer, and the qaghan's side won in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was given six targets and hit every deer; the qaghan's side won.

sentences.zh: 時有群飛，上曰：「公善彈，為我取之。」

translations.literal: At that time a flock was flying past; the emperor said, "You are skilled with the sling; fetch them for me."
translations.idiomatic: A flock of birds flew by; the emperor said, "You shoot well with the sling—bring them down for me."

sentences.zh: 十發俱中，並應丸而落。

translations.literal: Ten shots all struck home, each bird falling as the pellet answered.
translations.idiomatic: Ten shots all struck; every bird fell.

sentences.zh: 是日百官獲賚，晟獨居多。

translations.literal: That day the hundred officials received gifts, but Sheng alone received the greater share.
translations.idiomatic: That day the officials all received gifts, but Sheng received the largest share.

sentences.zh: 尋遣領五萬人，於朔州築大利城以處染幹。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent to lead fifty thousand men in building the great city of Dali at Shuozhou to settle Rangan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent with fifty thousand men to build the great city of Dali at Shuozhou to house Rangan.

sentences.zh: 安義公主死，持節送義城公主，複以妻之。

translations.literal: When Princess Anyi died, bearing credentials he escorted Princess Yicheng and again gave her in marriage to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Anyi died, he bore credentials, escorted Princess Yicheng, and gave her to Rangan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 晟又奏：「染幹部落歸者既眾，雖在長城之內，猶被雍閭抄略，往來辛苦，不得甯居。

translations.literal: Sheng again memorialized, "Rangan's returning tribes are already numerous; though they are within the Great Wall they still suffer Yonglu's raids; coming and going in hardship, they cannot live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized again, "Rangan's followers are already many; though inside the Great Wall they still suffer Yonglu's raids and cannot live in peace.

sentences.zh: 請徙五原，以河為固，于夏、勝兩州之間，東西至河，南北四百里，掘為橫塹，令處其內，任情放牧，免於抄略，人必自安。」

translations.literal: I beg that they be moved to Wuyuan, with the Yellow River as defense; between the two prefectures of Xia and Sheng, from the river east and west for four hundred li north and south, let a transverse trench be dug so that they dwell within it, grazing as they please, free from raids—then the people will surely settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Move them to Wuyuan with the Yellow River as rampart; between Xia and Sheng prefectures, four hundred li east to west and north to south along the river, dig a trench and let them pasture within it, safe from raids."

sentences.zh: 上並從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every point.

sentences.zh: 二十年，都藍大亂，為其部下所殺。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year Dulü fell into great disorder and was killed by his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year Dulü was thrown into turmoil and killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 晟因奏請曰：「今王師臨境，戰數有功，賊內攜離，其主被殺，乘此招誘，必並來降，請遣染幹部下分頭招慰。」

translations.literal: Sheng thereupon memorialized, "Now that the imperial army is on the frontier and has won repeated victories in battle, the enemy are divided within and their lord has been killed—seize this moment to entice them and they will surely all come to surrender; I beg that men of Rangan's following be sent in separate groups to win them over."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized, "Our army is on the frontier winning victories; the enemy are divided and their lord slain—send Rangan's men to win them over and they will all submit."

sentences.zh: 上許之，果盡來附。

translations.literal: The emperor consented, and indeed they all came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 達頭恐怖，又大集兵。

translations.literal: Datou was terrified and again gathered a great army.
translations.idiomatic: Datou was terrified and massed a great army again.

sentences.zh: 詔晟部領降人，為秦川行軍總管，取晉王廣節度出討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Sheng to command the surrendered men as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Qin River Circuit, taking Prince Guangs of Jin as commander and marching out to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was ordered to lead the surrendered Türks as campaigning commander-in-chief of the Qin River Circuit under Prince Guangs of Jin.

sentences.zh: 達頭與王相抗，晟進策曰：「突厥飲泉，易可行毒。」

translations.literal: Datou opposed the prince; Sheng advanced a stratagem, saying, "The Türks drink from springs; it is easy to poison them."
translations.idiomatic: Facing Datou, Sheng proposed, "The Türks drink from springs—it is easy to poison the water."

sentences.zh: 因取諸藥毒水上流，達頭人畜飲之多死，於是大驚曰：「天雨惡水，其亡我乎？」

translations.literal: They therefore took various drugs and poisoned the upstream water; Datou's men and beasts drank and many died; he was greatly alarmed and said, "Heaven rains evil water—is it destroying me?"
translations.idiomatic: Drugs were placed upstream; Datou's men and beasts drank and died in great numbers. In alarm he cried, "Heaven sends poisoned rain—has it forsaken me?"

sentences.zh: 因夜遁。

translations.literal: He therefore fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He fled in the night.

sentences.zh: 晟追之，斬首千餘級，俘百餘口，六畜數千頭。

translations.literal: Sheng pursued them, beheaded more than a thousand, captured more than a hundred persons, and took several thousand head of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng pursued him, took more than a thousand heads, captured over a hundred men, and seized thousands of livestock.

sentences.zh: 王大喜，引晟入內，同宴極歡。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and led Sheng inside, feasting together in the utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted, brought Sheng within, and feasted with him in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 有突厥達官來降，時亦預坐，說言突厥之內，大畏長孫總管，聞其弓聲，謂為霹靂，見其走馬，稱為閃電。

translations.literal: A Türk high official came to surrender and was also seated at the feast; he said that within the Türks they greatly feared Commander-in-Chief Zhangsun, that hearing his bow they called it thunder, and seeing his galloping horse they called it lightning.
translations.idiomatic: A surrendered Türk noble who shared the feast said the tribes greatly feared Commander Zhangsun—his bow sounded like thunder, his galloping horse like lightning.

sentences.zh: 王笑曰：「將軍震怒，威行域外，遂與雷霆為比，一何壯哉！」

translations.literal: The prince laughed and said, "The general's wrath shakes the realm beyond the borders and is compared with thunder—how magnificent!"
translations.idiomatic: The prince laughed and said, "Your anger, General, awes the outer realms and rivals the thunderclap—how splendid!"

sentences.zh: 師旋，授上開府儀同三司，複遣還大利城，安撫新附。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed Senior General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies and again sent back to the great city of Dali to pacify the newly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made Senior General-in-Chief with the ceremonial equipage of the Three Excellencies and sent back to Dali to pacify the new submissions.

sentences.zh: 仁壽元年，晟表奏曰：「臣夜登城樓，望見磧北有赤氣，長百餘裡，皆如雨足，下垂被地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Renshou, Sheng submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant climbed the city tower by night and saw north of the desert a red vapor more than a hundred li long, all like rain streaks hanging down to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou 1 (601) Sheng memorialized, "I climbed the city tower at night and saw north of the desert a red mist more than a hundred li long, hanging to earth like bloody rain.

sentences.zh: 謹驗兵書，此名灑血，其下之國必且破亡。

translations.literal: I have carefully checked the books of war: this is called 'spilled blood'; the state beneath it will surely be destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The military classics call this 'spilled blood'—the realm beneath it will fall.

sentences.zh: 欲滅匈奴，宜在今日。」

translations.literal: To destroy the Xiongnu, the time is today."
translations.idiomatic: If we mean to destroy the northern foe, the moment is now."

sentences.zh: 詔楊素為行軍元帥，晟為受降使者，送染幹北伐。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yang Su as campaigning commander-in-chief and Sheng as commissioner for receiving surrenders, escorting Rangan on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was made campaigning commander-in-chief and Sheng commissioner for receiving surrenders, escorting Rangan north.

sentences.zh: 二年，軍次北河，值賊帥思力俟斤等領兵拒戰，晟與大將軍梁默擊走之，轉戰六十餘裡，賊眾多降。

translations.literal: In the second year the army halted at the Northern River; it happened that the enemy commander Silijin and others led troops to resist; Sheng and the great general Liang Mo drove them off, fighting for more than sixty li, and many of the enemy surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the army reached the Northern River; the enemy commander Silijin and others resisted; Sheng and Grand General Liang Mo routed them after sixty li of fighting, and many surrendered.

sentences.zh: 晟又教染幹分遣使者，往北方鐵勒等部招攜取之。

translations.literal: Sheng also taught Rangan to send envoys in separate groups to the northern Tiele and other tribes to win them over and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng also had Rangan send envoys north to the Tiele and other tribes to win them over.

sentences.zh: 三年，有鐵勒、思結、伏利具、渾、斛薩、阿拔、僕骨等十餘部，盡背達頭，請來降附。

translations.literal: In the third year more than ten tribes including Tiele, Sijie, Fuliju, Hun, Husai, Abo, and Pugu all turned against Datou and asked to come surrender and attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year more than ten tribes—the Tiele, Sijie, Fuliju, Hun, Husai, Abo, Pugu, and others—all abandoned Datou and sought to submit.

sentences.zh: 達頭眾大潰，西奔吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Datou's masses collapsed in great rout and fled west to the Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Datou's forces collapsed and fled west to the Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 晟送染幹安置於磧口。

translations.literal: Sheng escorted Rangan and settled him at Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng escorted Rangan and settled him at Qikou.

sentences.zh: 事畢，入朝，遇高祖崩，匿喪未發。

translations.literal: When the affair was concluded he entered court and encountered the death of the High Ancestor; the mourning was concealed and not yet announced.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he returned to court just as Emperor Wen died; the death was kept secret and not yet announced.

sentences.zh: 煬帝引晟於大行前委以內衙宿衛，知門禁事，即日拜左領軍將軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang summoned Sheng before the bier and entrusted him with night guard in the inner palace, knowing matters of gates and barriers; that same day he was appointed General of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang took Sheng before the late emperor's bier and entrusted him with the inner palace guard and control of the gates; that day he was made General of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 遇楊諒作逆，敕以本官為相州刺史，發山東兵馬，與李雄等共經略之。

translations.literal: When Yang Liang rebelled, an edict ordered him, retaining his original office, to be Governor of Xiang Prefecture, to raise troops from Shandong, and together with Li Xiong and others to plan the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Liang rebelled, Sheng was ordered to remain in his post but become governor of Xiang Prefecture, raise Shandong troops, and plan the campaign with Li Xiong and others.

sentences.zh: 晟辭曰：「有男行布，今在逆地，忽蒙此任，情所不安。」

translations.literal: Sheng declined, saying, "I have a son, Xingbu, who is now in the rebel region; suddenly to receive this appointment is what my feelings cannot bear."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng declined: "My son Xingbu is in rebel territory; to accept this command unsettles me."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「公著勤誠，朕之所悉。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your loyal exertions are what We know well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your loyal service is well known to me.

sentences.zh: 今相州之地，本是齊都，人俗澆浮，易可搔擾。

translations.literal: The region of Xiang Prefecture was originally the capital of Qi; the people's customs are shallow and volatile, easily stirred to disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Prefecture was once the Qi capital; its people are fickle and easily stirred.

sentences.zh: 儻生變動，賊勢即張，思所以鎮之，非公莫可。

translations.literal: If trouble arises there, the rebels' power will immediately expand; We have thought how to hold it down, and no one but you will do.
translations.idiomatic: If trouble flares there the rebels will grow strong; only you can hold it.

sentences.zh: 公體國之深，終不可以兒害義，故用相委，公其勿辭。」

translations.literal: Your depth of concern for the state in the end cannot let a son harm righteousness; therefore We entrust this to you—do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty to the state must not let a son outweigh duty; I entrust this to you—do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 於是遣捉相州。

translations.literal: He was therefore sent to seize Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to take Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諒破，追還，轉武衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Liang was defeated Sheng was recalled and transferred to General of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was defeated he was recalled and made General of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，煬帝幸榆林，欲出塞外，陳兵耀武，經突厥中，指於涿郡。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, Emperor Yang visited Yulin and wished to go beyond the frontier, display troops and martial glory, pass through the Türk domain, and proceed to Zhuo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye 3 (607) Emperor Yang visited Yulin, planned to march beyond the border in full array through the Türk lands toward Zhuo commandery.

sentences.zh: 仍恐染幹驚懼，先遣晟往喻旨，稱述帝意。

translations.literal: Fearing that Rangan would be alarmed, he first sent Sheng ahead to explain the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Rangan would be alarmed, he sent Sheng ahead to explain the emperor's purpose.

sentences.zh: 染幹聽之，因召所部諸國，奚、霫、室韋等種落數十酋長咸萃。

translations.literal: Rangan heard this and therefore summoned the tribes under him; several tens of chieftains of the Xi, Mohe, Shiwei, and other peoples all gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan summoned the tribes under him; dozens of chieftains of the Xi, Mohe, Shiwei, and others assembled.

sentences.zh: 晟以牙中草穢，欲令染乾親自除之，示諸部落，以明威重，乃指帳前草曰：「此根大香。」

translations.literal: Sheng, because the grass within the headquarters was filthy, wished to have Rangan clear it himself to show the tribes and make clear his authority; he therefore pointed to the grass before the tent and said, "This root is very fragrant."
translations.idiomatic: The camp grass was foul; Sheng wished Rangan to clear it himself before the tribes to show imperial authority. Pointing at the grass before the tent he said, "This weed smells fine."

sentences.zh: 染幹遽嗅之曰：「殊不香也。」

translations.literal: Rangan hastily sniffed it and said, "It is not fragrant at all."
translations.idiomatic: Rangan sniffed and said, "It does not smell fine at all."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「天子行幸所在，諸侯躬親灑掃，耘除禦路，以表至敬之心。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven travels, the feudal lords personally sprinkle and sweep, hoe and clear the imperial road, to show the utmost sentiment of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Wherever the Son of Heaven travels, lords sweep the road themselves to show utmost respect.

sentences.zh: 今牙中蕪穢，謂是留香草耳。」

translations.literal: Now the headquarters are overgrown and rank—weeds left to grow, as it were."
translations.idiomatic: Your camp is overgrown—you have left weeds as if they were fragrant herbs."

sentences.zh: 染幹乃悟曰：「奴罪過。

translations.literal: Rangan then understood and said, "Your slave has sinned.
translations.idiomatic: Rangan understood: "Your slave has offended.

sentences.zh: 奴之骨肉，皆天子賜也，得效筋力，豈敢有辭？

translations.literal: My flesh and bone are all bestowed by the Son of Heaven; how could I dare refuse to exert sinew and bone?
translations.idiomatic: My very flesh and bone are the Son of Heaven's gift—how dare I refuse labor?

sentences.zh: 特以邊人不知法耳，賴將軍恩澤而教導之。

translations.literal: It is only that the frontier people do not know the law; relying on the general's grace and favor they are taught.
translations.idiomatic: Only the frontier folk do not know the law; they learn through your kindness.

sentences.zh: 將軍之惠，奴之幸也。」

translations.literal: The general's kindness is your slave's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Your kindness is my fortune."

sentences.zh: 遂拔所佩刀，親自芟草，其貴人及諸部爭放效之。

translations.literal: He thereupon drew the knife at his belt and personally cut the grass; his nobles and the various tribes vied to imitate him.
