translations.idiomatic: He drew his knife and cut the grass himself; nobles and tribes all followed.

sentences.zh: 乃發榆林北境，至於其牙，又東達於薊，長三千里，廣百步，舉國就役而開禦道。

translations.literal: They then set out from the northern border of Yulin as far as the headquarters, and eastward as far as Ji—a road three thousand li long and a hundred paces wide; the whole state took corvée labor and opened the imperial highway.
translations.idiomatic: From Yulin's northern border to the qaghan's camp and east to Ji they opened an imperial road three thousand li long and a hundred paces wide, the whole nation laboring at corvée.

sentences.zh: 帝聞晟策，乃益嘉焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of Sheng's stratagem he praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of Sheng's scheme and praised him the more.

sentences.zh: 後除淮陽太守，未赴任，複為右驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Huaiyang but did not take up the post; he was again made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Huaiyang but did not take up the post and was again made General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，時年五十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝深悼惜之，賵贈甚厚。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and regretted him; funeral gifts and grants were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him deeply and gave lavish funeral gifts.

sentences.zh: 後突厥圍雁門，帝歎曰：「向使長孫晟在，不令匈奴至此！」

translations.literal: Later, when the Türks besieged Yanmen, the emperor sighed and said, "If only Zhangsun Sheng were alive, he would not have let the Xiongnu come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Türks besieged Yanmen, the emperor sighed, "Had Zhangsun Sheng lived, the northern tribes would never have reached this!

sentences.zh: 晟好奇計，務功名。

translations.literal: Sheng delighted in ingenious stratagems and pursued fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng loved ingenious plans and pursued fame.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，居憂毀瘠，為朝士所稱。

translations.literal: By nature he was utterly filial; in mourning he wasted away, and the court gentlemen praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply filial; in mourning he wasted away, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，追贈司空、上柱國、齊國公，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Qi, with the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he was posthumously made Minister of Works, Supreme Pillar of State, and Duke of Qi, with the posthumous name Xian ("Accomplished").

sentences.zh: 少子無忌嗣。

translations.literal: His youngest son Wuji succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Wuji inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 其長子行布，亦多謀略，有父風。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xingbu was also full of stratagems and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xingbu was resourceful and had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 起家漢王諒庫真，甚見親狎。

translations.literal: He first entered service as a treasury attendant to Prince Han Liang and was greatly favored and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a treasury attendant to Prince Han Yang Liang and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 後遇諒於并州起逆，率眾南拒官軍，乃留行布城守，遂與豆盧毓等閉門拒諒，城陷，遇害。

translations.literal: Later, when Liang rebelled at Bing Prefecture, he led troops south to resist the imperial army; Xingbu was left to hold the city, and together with Dou Lu Yu and others he shut the gates to resist Liang; when the city fell he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang rebelled at Bing Prefecture, Xingbu held the city with Dou Lu Yu and others and resisted him; when the city fell he was killed.

sentences.zh: 次子恆安，以兄功授鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: The second son Heng'an, because of his brother's merit, was appointed General of the Hawkish Valor.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Heng'an, through his brother's service, was appointed General of the Hawkish Valor.

sentences.zh: 史評史臣曰：長孫氏爰自代陰，來儀京洛，門傳鍾鼎，家誓山河。

translations.literal: The historians comment: The house of Zhangsun, from Daiyin in their affection, came to measure their ritual at Luoyang; their gates transmitted bells and cauldrons, their house swore upon mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: The Zhangsun clan, beloved since the northern frontier, came to establish ritual at Luoyang; their house bore noble emblems and bound itself to the realm.

sentences.zh: 漢代八王，無以方其茂績；

translations.literal: The eight kings of Han cannot match their lush achievements;
translations.idiomatic: The eight kings of Han cannot equal their flourishing merit;

sentences.zh: 張氏七葉，不能譬此重光。

translations.literal: the seven generations of Zhang cannot be compared with this doubled glory.
translations.idiomatic: the seven generations of the Zhang clan cannot match this renewed splendor.

sentences.zh: 覽獨擅雄辨，熾早稱爽俊，俱司禮閣，並統師旅，且公且侯，文武不墜。

translations.literal: Lan alone excelled in forceful disputation, Chi was early called bright and outstanding; both held office in the Ritual Pavilion and both commanded armies—dukes and marquises, civil and military without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Lan alone excelled in eloquence, Chi was praised early for brilliance; both served in the Ritual Offices and both commanded armies—civil and martial glory undiminished.

sentences.zh: 晟體資英武，兼包奇略，因機制變，懷彼戎夷。

translations.literal: Sheng's endowment was heroic and martial, embracing extraordinary stratagems; he adapted to opportunity and won over those frontier peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was heroic and resourceful, adapting to circumstance and mastering the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 傾巢盡落，屈膝稽顙，塞垣絕鳴鏑之旅，渭橋有單于之拜。

translations.literal: Their nests were overturned and all fell; they bent the knee and knocked the forehead; on the frontier the clatter of bowstrings ceased, and at the Wei Bridge there was the khan's bow.
translations.idiomatic: He overturned their nests until they knelt in submission; the frontier fell silent of bowstrings, and at the Wei Bridge the qaghan paid homage.

sentences.zh: 惠流邊朔，功光王府，保茲爵祿，不亦宜乎！

translations.literal: His grace flowed to the northern marches and his merit shone upon the royal house—was it not fitting that he preserve rank and emolument!
translations.idiomatic: His grace reached the northern border and his merit lit the imperial house—was it not right that he keep rank and reward!
